steps.body: The zero-one-two story replays on the circle, and horizontal lines tell it cleanest. y = 3 in x² + y² = 25 leaves x² = 16: two punctures. y = 5 leaves x² = 0: one touch — tangent at the very top. y = 6 leaves x² = −11: impossible, a miss.

explanationVariants: y = 3 gives x² = 25 − 9 = 16, so x = ±4: crossings (−4, 3) and (4, 3).
Height 3 is inside the radius, so the line cuts a chord with two ends.

widget.prompt: y = 3 meets x² + y² = 25 where x² = 16. How many intersection points?

commonErrors.feedback: x = +4 AND x = −4 both work — the horizontal line enters and exits.
Each root is one point on THIS line; the count is 2, not 4.

widget.fallbackFeedback: x² = 16 gives x = ±4 — two symmetric points, (4, 3) and (−4, 3).

explanationVariants: y = 5 forces x² = 0 — the single point (0, 5), where the line grazes the circle's crown.
x² = 0 has one root, doubled: tangency at the topmost point.

widget.prompt: y = 5 meets x² + y² = 25 where x² = 0. Geometrically the line…

options.label: Is tangent at (0, 5)
options.feedback: The one doubled root is the circle's north pole — the line rests on the crown.

options.label: Crosses at two points
options.feedback: Two crossings need x² > 0; zero has a single root.

options.label: Misses entirely
options.feedback: A miss needs x² NEGATIVE; zero still yields the point (0, 5).

widget.prompt: Each horizontal line meets x² + y² = 25 how many times? Compute x² = 25 − k² and sort.

items.label: y = 0
items.feedback: y = 0 is the diameter line: x² = 25 gives ±5 — two points.

items.label: y = 4
items.feedback: y = 4: x² = 9 gives ±3 — still two, the chord is just shorter.

items.label: y = 5
items.feedback: y = 5 grazes the top: x² = 0 has one answer — tangent.

items.label: y = −5
items.feedback: y = −5 grazes the bottom — one point, tangent again.

items.label: y = 7
items.feedback: y = 7: x² = 25 − 49 < 0 — no real x, the line sails above the circle.

widget.missFeedback: x² = 25 − k²: positive → two, zero → one, negative → none. Compare each |k| with the radius 5.
widget.successFeedback: Heights inside the radius cut chords (y = 0 is the widest — the diameter), |k| = 5 grazes top and bottom, and y = 7 sails over. The radius is the whole verdict: |k| vs 5.

steps.body: One chord point, placed by hand.

widget.prompt: k1's chord: y = 3 meets x² + y² = 25 where x² = 16. Plot the first-quadrant intersection.

pointErrors.feedback: Coordinates swapped — that is the y = 4 chord's point. Here y = 3 is fixed and x² = 16.
x = 5 only happens at y = 0: check 25 + 9 = 34 ≠ 25. The radius budget is already spent.

widget.missFeedback: With y = 3 the circle demands x² = 25 − 9 = 16, so the first-quadrant point is (4, 3).
widget.successFeedback: (4, 3): 16 + 9 = 25 exactly — on the circle AND on the line, one of the chord's two crossings.

predict.prompt: Without computing: y = −5 will meet the circle how many times?
predict.reveal: By symmetry with y = 5 — it grazes the BOTTOM at (0, −5), since x² = 25 − 25 = 0 again. The circle treats up and down alike; every tangent height has a mirror twin.

steps.body: The pattern in one sentence: a horizontal line y = k meets the radius-5 circle twice when |k| < 5, once when |k| = 5, never when |k| > 5. Distance-to-center against radius — the same three-way comparison the discriminant made for parabolas, wearing geometric clothes.

explanationVariants: |−2| = 2 < 5, so y = −2 cuts a chord: two points, at x = ±√21.
Height 2 below center is still inside the radius — two crossings.

widget.prompt: How many times does y = −2 meet x² + y² = 25?

options.label: Twice — |−2| < 5
options.feedback: x² = 21 > 0: two roots, a chord below the middle.

options.label: Once — negative heights are tangent
options.feedback: Tangency needs |k| EQUAL to 5; 2 is well inside.

options.label: Never — the circle stops at y = 0
options.feedback: The circle spans y from −5 to 5; its lower half is half the rim.

explanationVariants: y = x + c into the circle gives 2x² + 2cx + c² − 25 = 0; discriminant 4c² − 8(c² − 25) = 200 − 4c², zero at c² = 50 — c = √50 ≈ 7.07.
Tangency for the tilted line lands at c = ±√50, just past 7 — farther out than the horizontal tangent's 5, because the line meets the circle diagonally.
hints: Substitute y = x + c: 2x² + 2cx + (c² − 25) = 0. Write the discriminant.
c² = 50, so the positive c is √50 ≈ 7.07 — enter it to one decimal.

widget.prompt: For what positive c (one decimal) is y = x + c tangent to x² + y² = 25?

commonErrors.feedback: 5 is the HORIZONTAL tangent height; a tilted line stays farther out — c = √50 ≈ 7.1.
50 is c²; the tangent offset is its root, ≈ 7.1.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Tangency puts the line at distance 5 from the center: |c|/√2 = 5, so c = 5√2 ≈ 7.1.

takeaways: |height| vs radius: under cuts, equal grazes, over misses.
Tangency is the doubled root again — x² = 0 or discriminant 0.
Tilted lines answer to the same discriminant as parabolas did.
steps.teaser: next course idea: the bell curve — where piles of chance take a predictable shape.
